text.tspan: Where latency comes from: four delays, added on every hop
push the bits onto the wire
RTT = round-trip time: there AND back (ping shows it)
HTTPS needs about 2 round trips (TCP + TLS 1.3)
before the request: at 200 ms RTT that's 400 ms;
a CDN edge 10 ms away does it in 20 ms.
Distance sets a floor no bandwidth can beat
one way ≥ 13,000 × 5 µs = 65 ms, so RTT ≥ 130 ms
real RTTs are higher: cables don't run straight
A faster link shrinks (1) transmission but never (2) propagation: only moving closer does that.
